subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that cot(π/20) · cot(3π/20) · cot(5π/20) · cot(7π/20) · cot(9π/20) = 1.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Convert to degrees and pair
steps.margin_note: Degrees make the pattern easy to read. Bracket the first factor with the last and the second with the fourth; cot 45° is left in the middle.

recall.must_convey: That the angles are 9°, 27°, 45°, 63°, 81° and that they are paired from the two ends.
accept: multiply pi by twenty by nine to get nine degrees and pair the first with the last
the angles are nine twenty seven forty five sixty three and eighty one degrees
pair the outer factors and leave forty five in the middle
degrees lo rasi, first and last pair chesi forty five middle lo undipoyindi
there are five factors so one stays alone

steps.why: Each bracketed pair of angles adds to 90°, so the two angles in a pair are complementary. Pairing from the two ends is the only arrangement that gives this.
common_mistakes: Pairing neighbouring factors instead of pairing from the two ends.
Dropping the middle factor cot 45° while bracketing.
steps.memory_tip: Five factors, so one is left over: first with last, second with fourth, and 45° alone.

steps.label: Rewrite the two larger angles
steps.margin_note: First mark. Turn cot 81° into tan 9° and cot 63° into tan 27°, and write cot 45° = 1.

recall.must_convey: That each larger angle is written as 90° minus the smaller, so its cotangent becomes the tangent of the smaller, and cot 45° = 1.
accept: eighty one is ninety minus nine so cot eighty one is tan nine
cot of ninety minus theta is tan theta
the larger angle in each bracket is the complement of the smaller one
cot ninety minus theta ante tan theta, and cot forty five is one
change each larger cotangent into a tangent

steps.why: In each bracket the larger angle is 90° minus the smaller one, so its cotangent becomes the tangent of the smaller angle.
common_mistakes: Writing cot(90° − θ) as cot θ.
Forgetting that the middle factor cot 45° is 1.
steps.memory_tip: cot(90° − θ) = tan θ. The larger angle of each pair is 90° minus the smaller one.

steps.label: Use cot θ · tan θ = 1
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Each bracket is a cotangent times its own tangent, which is 1, and the middle factor is 1, so the whole product is 1.
lines: cot θ · tan θ = 1 for every angle θ

recall.must_convey: That each bracket gives cot θ · tan θ = 1, so the whole product is 1.
accept: cot theta times tan theta is one so every bracket is one
each bracket reduces to one and the answer is one
they are reciprocals so the product is one
cot and tan reciprocals, so product one
the value of the whole product is one
reject: change each larger cotangent into a tangent

steps.why: cot θ and tan θ are reciprocals, so their product is 1 wherever both are defined. No angle has to be worked out as a number.
common_mistakes: Working out each cotangent as a decimal.
Writing cot θ · tan θ as tan²θ.
steps.memory_tip: cot θ and tan θ are reciprocals, so each bracket is exactly 1.
